title: Name That Method
instruction: Which signal is this recommendation built on?

items.text: Fans of this artist also listen to…
items.why: Built from what other people co-consume, not from what the music sounds like.

items.text: Customers who bought this also bought…
items.why: Item-to-item collaborative filtering: co-purchases by other customers.

items.text: People whose ratings track yours loved this film
items.why: User-to-user collaborative filtering: find taste neighbours, borrow their opinions.

items.text: Same author, same genre, similar description
items.why: Item features only: no other users needed.

items.text: A podcast published an hour ago, matched to you by its transcript topics
items.why: Content works on day one, before anyone has listened: the answer to item cold start.

items.text: Laptops with the same screen size, processor and price range
items.why: Matching on specifications is matching on item attributes.
The same list for everyone in the country: no personal taste involved.
A ranking by volume, identical for every user.

items.text: A visitor with no account views three tents; the next suggestion is a sleeping pad
items.why: Only the clicks of this visit are known, so their order drives the next suggestion.

items.text: The next song is chosen from the order of your last five plays
items.why: A sequence model reads what you just did, in order.

debrief: Production systems blend all four: popularity as a safe default, content for new items, collaborative signal once behaviour accumulates, and the current session for what you want right now.
